# Part II: Getting and Shaping Data {.unnumbered}

Before any analysis, the data has to be read, cleaned and put into shape. In audit this is often most of the work, because auditees rarely send data in a form ready for analysis. This part covers every step: organising files, reading CSV and Excel files and the awkward ones, PDFs and spreadsheets laid out for printing; cleaning; combining many files into one; transforming, joining and reshaping tables; working with dates and times; and handling data too large for Excel.

The tidyverse packages, dplyr and tidyr above all, are the tools of this part, and of the rest of the book.

The chapters in this part are:

- @sec-file, files and folders, and fixing the data received with a hash.
- @sec-read, reading and writing CSV and Excel files, and checking what was read.
- @sec-clean, cleaning names, blanks, types and inconsistent entries.
- @sec-pdfxl, data from PDFs and from messy Excel workbooks.
- @sec-merge, combining many similar files into one.
- @sec-DPLYRR, filtering, summarising and transforming data with dplyr.
- @sec-joins, joining tables, and the audit tests built on joins.
- @sec-tidyr, reshaping data between wide and long forms.
- @sec-lubridate, dates and times, financial years, ageing and off-hours analysis.
- @sec-duckdb, data larger than Excel, with DuckDB and data.table.
